12 /-!
13 # Cardinality of a finite set
14 
15 This defines the cardinality of a `Finset` and provides induction principles for finsets.
16 
17 ## Main declarations
18 
19 * `Finset.card`: `#s : ℕ` returns the cardinality of `s : Finset α`.
20 
21 ### Induction principles
22 
23 * `Finset.strongInduction`: Strong induction
24 * `Finset.strongInductionOn`
25 * `Finset.strongDownwardInduction`
26 * `Finset.strongDownwardInductionOn`
27 * `Finset.case_strong_induction_on`
28 * `Finset.Nonempty.strong_induction`
29 * `Finset.eraseInduction`
30 -/

44 /-- `s.card` is the number of elements of `s`, aka its cardinality.
45 
46 The notation `#s` can be accessed in the `Finset` locale. -/
47 def card (s : Finset α) : ℕ :=
48   Multiset.card s.1
49 
50 @[inherit_doc] scoped prefix:arg "#" => Finset.card
51 
52 theorem card_def (s : Finset α) : #s = Multiset.card s.1 :=
53   rfl
54 
55 @[simp] lemma card_val (s : Finset α) : Multiset.card s.1 = #s := rfl
56 
57 @[simp]
58 theorem card_mk {m nodup} : #(⟨m, nodup⟩ : Finset α) = Multiset.card m :=
59   rfl
60

62 theorem card_empty : #(∅ : Finset α) = 0 :=
63   rfl

66 theorem card_le_card : s ⊆ t → #s ≤ #t :=
67   Multiset.card_le_card ∘ val_le_iff.mpr

71 local grind_pattern card_le_card => #s, #t

76 @[simp] lemma card_eq_zero : #s = 0 ↔ s = ∅ := Multiset.card_eq_zero.trans val_eq_zero
77 lemma card_ne_zero : #s ≠ 0 ↔ s.Nonempty := card_eq_zero.ne.trans nonempty_iff_ne_empty.symm
78 @[simp] lemma card_pos : 0 < #s ↔ s.Nonempty := Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero.trans card_ne_zero
79 @[simp] lemma one_le_card : 1 ≤ #s ↔ s.Nonempty := card_pos

225 theorem injOn_of_card_image_eq [DecidableEq β] (H : #(s.image f) = #s) : Set.InjOn f s := by
226   rw [card_def, card_def, image, toFinset] at H
227   dsimp only at H
228   have : (s.1.map f).dedup = s.1.map f := by
229     refine Multiset.eq_of_le_of_card_le (Multiset.dedup_le _) ?_

231   rw [Multiset.dedup_eq_self] at this

248 lemma card_filter_le_iff (s : Finset α) (P : α → Prop) [DecidablePred P] (n : ℕ) :
249     #(s.filter P) ≤ n ↔ ∀ s' ⊆ s, n < #s' → ∃ a ∈ s', ¬ P a :=
250   (s.1.card_filter_le_iff P n).trans ⟨fun H s' hs' h ↦ H s'.1 (by simp_all) h,
251     fun H s' hs' h ↦ H ⟨s', nodup_of_le hs' s.2⟩ (fun _ hx ↦ Multiset.subset_of_le hs' hx) h⟩
252

254 theorem card_map (f : α ↪ β) : #(s.map f) = #s :=
255   Multiset.card_map _ _

259     #(s.subtype p) = #(s.filter p) := by simp [Finset.subtype]
260 
261 theorem card_filter_le (s : Finset α) (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p] :
262     #(s.filter p) ≤ #s :=

265 grind_pattern card_filter_le => #(s.filter p)

268 theorem eq_of_subset_of_card_le {s t : Finset α} (h : s ⊆ t) (h₂ : #t ≤ #s) : s = t :=
269   eq_of_veq <| Multiset.eq_of_le_of_card_le (val_le_iff.mpr h) h₂
270 
271 theorem eq_iff_card_le_of_subset (hst : s ⊆ t) : #t ≤ #s ↔ s = t :=
272   ⟨eq_of_subset_of_card_le hst, (ge_of_eq <| congr_arg _ ·)⟩

274 theorem eq_of_superset_of_card_ge (hst : s ⊆ t) (hts : #t ≤ #s) : t = s :=
275   (eq_of_subset_of_card_le hst hts).symm

278   (eq_iff_card_le_of_subset hst).trans eq_comm

280 theorem subset_iff_eq_of_card_le (h : #t ≤ #s) : s ⊆ t ↔ s = t :=

283 theorem map_eq_of_subset {f : α ↪ α} (hs : s.map f ⊆ s) : s.map f = s :=
284   eq_of_subset_of_card_le hs (card_map _).ge

286 theorem card_filter_eq_iff {p : α → Prop} [DecidablePred p] :
287     #(s.filter p) = #s ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, p x := by
288   rw [← (card_filter_le s p).ge_iff_eq, eq_iff_card_le_of_subset (filter_subset p s),

294     #(s.filter p) = 0 ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, ¬ p x := by

302 section bij

304 /--
305 See also `card_bij`.
306 TODO: consider deprecating, since this has been unused in mathlib for a long time and is just a
307 special case of `card_bij`.
308 -/
309 theorem card_eq_of_bijective (f : ∀ i, i < n → α) (hf : ∀ a ∈ s, ∃ i, ∃ h : i < n, f i h = a)
310     (hf' : ∀ i (h : i < n), f i h ∈ s)
311     (f_inj : ∀ i j (hi : i < n) (hj : j < n), f i hi = f j hj → i = j) : #s = n := by
312   classical
313   have : s = (range n).attach.image fun i => f i.1 (mem_range.1 i.2) := by
314     ext a
315     suffices _ : a ∈ s ↔ ∃ (i : _) (hi : i ∈ range n), f i (mem_range.1 hi) = a by
316       simpa only [mem_image, mem_attach, true_and, Subtype.exists]
317     constructor
318     · intro ha; obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := hf a ha; use i, mem_range.2 hi
319     · rintro ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩; apply hf'
320   calc
321     #s = #((range n).attach.image fun i => f i.1 (mem_range.1 i.2)) := by rw [this]
322     _ = #(range n).attach := ?_
323     _ = #(range n) := card_attach
324     _ = n := card_range n
325   apply card_image_of_injective
326   intro ⟨i, hi⟩ ⟨j, hj⟩ eq
327   exact Subtype.ext <| f_inj i j (mem_range.1 hi) (mem_range.1 hj) eq
328 
329 variable {t : Finset β}
330 
331 /-- Given a bijection from a finite set `s` to a finite set `t`, the cardinalities of `s` and `t`
332 are equal.
333 
334 The difference with `Finset.card_bij'` is that the bijection is specified as a surjective injection,
335 rather than by an inverse function.
336 
337 The difference with `Finset.card_nbij` is that the bijection is allowed to use membership of the
338 domain, rather than being a non-dependent function. -/
339 lemma card_bij (i : ∀ a ∈ s, β) (hi : ∀ a ha, i a ha ∈ t)
340     (i_inj : ∀ a₁ ha₁ a₂ ha₂, i a₁ ha₁ = i a₂ ha₂ → a₁ = a₂)
341     (i_surj : ∀ b ∈ t, ∃ a ha, i a ha = b) : #s = #t := by
342   classical
343   calc
344     #s = #s.attach := card_attach.symm
345     _ = #(s.attach.image fun a ↦ i a.1 a.2) := Eq.symm ?_
346     _ = #t := ?_
347   · apply card_image_of_injective
348     intro ⟨_, _⟩ ⟨_, _⟩ h
349     simpa using i_inj _ _ _ _ h
350   · congr 1
351     ext b
352     constructor <;> intro h
353     · obtain ⟨_, _, rfl⟩ := mem_image.1 h; apply hi
354     · obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := i_surj b h; exact mem_image.2 ⟨⟨a, ha⟩, by simp⟩
355 
356 /-- Given a bijection from a finite set `s` to a finite set `t`, the cardinalities of `s` and `t`
357 are equal.
358 
359 The difference with `Finset.card_bij` is that the bijection is specified with an inverse, rather
360 than as a surjective injection.
361 
362 The difference with `Finset.card_nbij'` is that the bijection and its inverse are allowed to use
363 membership of the domains, rather than being non-dependent functions. -/
364 lemma card_bij' (i : ∀ a ∈ s, β) (j : ∀ a ∈ t, α) (hi : ∀ a ha, i a ha ∈ t)
365     (hj : ∀ a ha, j a ha ∈ s) (left_inv : ∀ a ha, j (i a ha) (hi a ha) = a)
366     (right_inv : ∀ a ha, i (j a ha) (hj a ha) = a) : #s = #t := by
367   refine card_bij i hi (fun a1 h1 a2 h2 eq ↦ ?_) (fun b hb ↦ ⟨_, hj b hb, right_inv b hb⟩)
368   rw [← left_inv a1 h1, ← left_inv a2 h2]
369   simp only [eq]
370 
371 /-- Given a bijection from a finite set `s` to a finite set `t`, the cardinalities of `s` and `t`
372 are equal.
373 
374 The difference with `Finset.card_nbij'` is that the bijection is specified as a surjective
375 injection, rather than by an inverse function.
376 
377 The difference with `Finset.card_bij` is that the bijection is a non-dependent function, rather than
378 being allowed to use membership of the domain. -/
379 lemma card_nbij (i : α → β) (hi : Set.MapsTo i s t) (i_inj : (s : Set α).InjOn i)
380     (i_surj : (s : Set α).SurjOn i t) : #s = #t :=
381   card_bij (fun a _ ↦ i a) hi i_inj (by simpa using i_surj)
382 
383 /-- Given a bijection from a finite set `s` to a finite set `t`, the cardinalities of `s` and `t`
384 are equal.
385 
386 The difference with `Finset.card_nbij` is that the bijection is specified with an inverse, rather
387 than as a surjective injection.
388 
389 The difference with `Finset.card_bij'` is that the bijection and its inverse are non-dependent
390 functions, rather than being allowed to use membership of the domains.
391 
392 The difference with `Finset.card_equiv` is that bijectivity is only required to hold on the domains,
393 rather than on the entire types. -/
394 lemma card_nbij' (i : α → β) (j : β → α) (hi : Set.MapsTo i s t) (hj : Set.MapsTo j t s)
395     (left_inv : Set.LeftInvOn j i s) (right_inv : Set.RightInvOn j i t) : #s = #t :=
396   card_bij' (fun a _ ↦ i a) (fun b _ ↦ j b) hi hj left_inv right_inv
397 
398 /-- Specialization of `Finset.card_nbij'` that automatically fills in most arguments.
399 
400 See `Fintype.card_equiv` for the version where `s` and `t` are `univ`. -/
401 lemma card_equiv (e : α ≃ β) (hst : ∀ i, i ∈ s ↔ e i ∈ t) : #s = #t := by
402   refine card_nbij' e e.symm ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ <;> simp [hst, Set.MapsTo, Set.LeftInvOn, Set.RightInvOn]
403 
404 /-- Specialization of `Finset.card_nbij` that automatically fills in most arguments.
405 
406 See `Fintype.card_bijective` for the version where `s` and `t` are `univ`. -/
407 lemma card_bijective (e : α → β) (he : e.Bijective) (hst : ∀ i, i ∈ s ↔ e i ∈ t) :
408     #s = #t := card_equiv (.ofBijective e he) hst
409 
410 lemma _root_.Set.BijOn.finsetCard_eq (e : α → β) (he : Set.BijOn e s t) : #s = #t :=
411   card_nbij e he.mapsTo he.injOn he.surjOn
412 
413 lemma card_le_card_of_injOn (f : α → β) (hf : Set.MapsTo f s t) (f_inj : (s : Set α).InjOn f) :
414     #s ≤ #t := by
415   classical
416   calc
417     #s = #(s.image f) := (card_image_of_injOn f_inj).symm
418     _ ≤ #t := card_le_card <| image_subset_iff.2 hf
419 
420 lemma card_le_card_of_injective {f : s → t} (hf : f.Injective) : #s ≤ #t := by
421   rcases s.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | ⟨a₀, ha₀⟩
422   · simp
423   · classical
424     let f' : α → β := fun a => f (if ha : a ∈ s then ⟨a, ha⟩ else ⟨a₀, ha₀⟩)
425     apply card_le_card_of_injOn f'
426     · aesop (add safe unfold Set.MapsTo)
427     · intro a₁ ha₁ a₂ ha₂ haa
428       rw [mem_coe] at ha₁ ha₂
429       simp only [f', ha₁, ha₂, ← Subtype.ext_iff] at haa
430       exact Subtype.ext_iff.mp (hf haa)
431 
432 grind_pattern card_le_card_of_injective => f.Injective, #s
433 grind_pattern card_le_card_of_injective => f.Injective, #t
434 
435 lemma card_le_card_of_surjOn (f : α → β) (hf : Set.SurjOn f s t) : #t ≤ #s := by
436   classical unfold Set.SurjOn at hf; exact (card_le_card (mod_cast hf)).trans card_image_le
437 
438 /-- If there are more pigeons than pigeonholes, then there are two pigeons in the same pigeonhole.
439 
440 See also `Set.exists_ne_map_eq_of_encard_lt_of_maps_to` and
441 `Set.exists_ne_map_eq_of_ncard_lt_of_maps_to`. -/
442 theorem exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt_of_maps_to (hc : #t < #s) {f : α → β}
443     (hf : Set.MapsTo f s t) : ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ s, x ≠ y ∧ f x = f y := by
444   classical
445   by_contra! hz
446   refine hc.not_ge (card_le_card_of_injOn f hf ?_)
447   intro x hx y hy
448   contrapose
449   exact hz x hx y hy
450 
451 /-- a special case of `Finset.exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt_of_maps_to` where `t` is `s.image f` -/
452 theorem exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_image_lt [DecidableEq β] {f : α → β} (hc : #(s.image f) < #s) :
453     ∃ x ∈ s, ∃ y ∈ s, x ≠ y ∧ f x = f y :=
454   exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt_of_maps_to hc (coe_image (β := β) ▸ Set.mapsTo_image f s)
455 
456 /-- a variant of `Finset.exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_image_lt` using `Set.InjOn` -/
457 theorem not_injOn_of_card_image_lt [DecidableEq β] {f : α → β} (hc : #(s.image f) < #s) :
458     ¬ Set.InjOn f s :=
459   mt card_image_of_injOn hc.ne
460 
461 /--
462 See also `Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn`, which is a more general version of this lemma.
463 TODO: consider deprecating, since this is just a special case of `Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn`.
464 -/
465 lemma le_card_of_inj_on_range (f : ℕ → α) (hf : ∀ i < n, f i ∈ s)
466     (f_inj : ∀ i < n, ∀ j < n, f i = f j → i = j) : n ≤ #s :=
467   calc
468     n = #(range n) := (card_range n).symm
469     _ ≤ #s := card_le_card_of_injOn f (by simpa [Set.MapsTo, mem_range] using hf) (by simpa)
470 
471 /--
472 Given an injective map `f` from a finite set `s` to another finite set `t`, if `t` is no larger
473 than `s`, then `f` is surjective to `t` when restricted to `s`.
474 See `Finset.surj_on_of_inj_on_of_card_le` for the version where `f` is a dependent function.
475 -/
476 lemma surjOn_of_injOn_of_card_le (f : α → β) (hf : Set.MapsTo f s t) (hinj : Set.InjOn f s)
477     (hst : #t ≤ #s) : Set.SurjOn f s t := by
478   classical
479   suffices s.image f = t by simp [← this, Set.SurjOn]
480   have : s.image f ⊆ t := by aesop (add simp Finset.subset_iff)
481   exact eq_of_subset_of_card_le this (hst.trans_eq (card_image_of_injOn hinj).symm)
482 
483 /--
484 Given an injective map `f` defined on a finite set `s` to another finite set `t`, if `t` is no
485 larger than `s`, then `f` is surjective to `t` when restricted to `s`.
486 See `Finset.surjOn_of_injOn_of_card_le` for the version where `f` is a non-dependent function.
487 -/
488 lemma surj_on_of_inj_on_of_card_le (f : ∀ a ∈ s, β) (hf : ∀ a ha, f a ha ∈ t)
489     (hinj : ∀ a₁ a₂ ha₁ ha₂, f a₁ ha₁ = f a₂ ha₂ → a₁ = a₂) (hst : #t ≤ #s) :
490     ∀ b ∈ t, ∃ a ha, b = f a ha := by
491   let f' : s → β := fun a ↦ f a a.2
492   have hinj' : Set.InjOn f' s.attach := fun x hx y hy hxy ↦ Subtype.ext (hinj _ _ x.2 y.2 hxy)
493   have hmapsto' : Set.MapsTo f' s.attach t := fun x hx ↦ hf _ _
494   intro b hb
495   obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := surjOn_of_injOn_of_card_le _ hmapsto' hinj' (by rwa [card_attach]) hb
496   exact ⟨a, a.2, rfl⟩
497 
498 /--
499 Given a surjective map `f` from a finite set `s` to another finite set `t`, if `s` is no larger
500 than `t`, then `f` is injective when restricted to `s`.
501 See `Finset.inj_on_of_surj_on_of_card_le` for the version where `f` is a dependent function.
502 -/
503 lemma injOn_of_surjOn_of_card_le (f : α → β) (hf : Set.MapsTo f s t) (hsurj : Set.SurjOn f s t)
504     (hst : #s ≤ #t) : Set.InjOn f s := by
505   classical
506   have : s.image f = t := Finset.coe_injective <| by simp [hsurj.image_eq_of_mapsTo hf]
507   have : #(s.image f) = #t := by rw [this]
508   have : #(s.image f) ≤ #s := card_image_le
509   rw [← card_image_iff]
510   lia
511 
512 /--
513 Given a surjective map `f` defined on a finite set `s` to another finite set `t`, if `s` is no
514 larger than `t`, then `f` is injective when restricted to `s`.
515 See `Finset.injOn_of_surjOn_of_card_le` for the version where `f` is a non-dependent function.
516 -/
517 theorem inj_on_of_surj_on_of_card_le (f : ∀ a ∈ s, β) (hf : ∀ a ha, f a ha ∈ t)
518     (hsurj : ∀ b ∈ t, ∃ a ha, f a ha = b) (hst : #s ≤ #t) ⦃a₁⦄ (ha₁ : a₁ ∈ s) ⦃a₂⦄
519     (ha₂ : a₂ ∈ s) (ha₁a₂ : f a₁ ha₁ = f a₂ ha₂) : a₁ = a₂ := by
520   let f' : s → β := fun a ↦ f a a.2
521   have hsurj' : Set.SurjOn f' s.attach t := fun x hx ↦ by simpa [f'] using hsurj x hx
522   have hinj' := injOn_of_surjOn_of_card_le f' (fun x hx ↦ hf _ _) hsurj' (by simpa)
523   exact congrArg Subtype.val (@hinj' ⟨a₁, ha₁⟩ (by simp) ⟨a₂, ha₂⟩ (by simp) ha₁a₂)
524 
525 end bij
526 
527 @[simp, grind =]
528 theorem card_disjUnion (s t : Finset α) (h) : #(s.disjUnion t h) = #s + #t :=
529   Multiset.card_add _ _

620 /-- **Pigeonhole principle** for two finsets inside an ambient finset. -/
621 theorem inter_nonempty_of_card_lt_card_add_card (hts : t ⊆ s) (hus : u ⊆ s)
622     (hstu : #s < #t + #u) : (t ∩ u).Nonempty := by
623   contrapose! hstu
624   calc
625     _ = #(t ∪ u) := by simp [← card_union_add_card_inter, hstu]
626     _ ≤ #s := by gcongr; exact union_subset hts hus

639 /-- Given a subset `s` of a set `t`, of sizes at most and at least `n` respectively, there exists a
640 set `u` of size `n` which is both a superset of `s` and a subset of `t`. -/
641 lemma exists_subsuperset_card_eq (hst : s ⊆ t) (hsn : #s ≤ n) (hnt : n ≤ #t) :
642     ∃ u, s ⊆ u ∧ u ⊆ t ∧ #u = n := by
643   classical
644   refine Nat.decreasingInduction' ?_ hnt ⟨t, by simp [hst]⟩
645   intro k _ hnk ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂, hu₃⟩
646   obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ : (u \ s).Nonempty := by grind
647   exact ⟨u.erase a, by grind⟩
648 
649 /-- We can shrink a set to any smaller size. -/
650 lemma exists_subset_card_eq (hns : n ≤ #s) : ∃ t ⊆ s, #t = n := by
651   simpa using exists_subsuperset_card_eq s.empty_subset (by simp) hns
652 
653 theorem le_card_iff_exists_subset_card : n ≤ #s ↔ ∃ t ⊆ s, #t = n := by
654   refine ⟨fun h => ?_, fun ⟨t, hst, ht⟩ => ht ▸ card_le_card hst⟩
655   exact exists_subset_card_eq h

658     (hXY : 2 * n < #(X ∪ Y)) : ∃ C : Finset α, n < #C ∧ (C ⊆ X ∨ C ⊆ Y) := by
659   grind =>
660     have : #(X ∪ Y) = #X + #(Y \ X)
661     finish

666 theorem card_eq_one : #s = 1 ↔ ∃ a, s = {a} := by
667   cases s
668   simp only [Multiset.card_eq_one, Finset.card, ← val_inj, singleton_val]
669 
670 theorem exists_eq_insert_iff [DecidableEq α] {s t : Finset α} :
671     (∃ a ∉ s, insert a s = t) ↔ s ⊆ t ∧ #s + 1 = #t := by
672   constructor
673   · grind
674   · rintro ⟨hst, h⟩
675     obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ : ∃ a, t \ s = {a} := card_eq_one.mp (by grind)
676     grind =>
677       have : a ∈ t \ s
678       have h : insert a s ⊆ t
679       have := eq_of_subset_of_card_le h
680       instantiate

682 theorem card_le_one : #s ≤ 1 ↔ ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ s, a = b := by
683   obtain rfl | ⟨x, hx⟩ := s.eq_empty_or_nonempty
684   · simp
685   refine (Nat.succ_le_of_lt (card_pos.2 ⟨x, hx⟩)).ge_iff_eq'.trans (card_eq_one.trans ⟨?_, ?_⟩)
686   · grind
687   · exact fun h => ⟨x, by grind⟩
688 
689 theorem card_le_one_iff : #s ≤ 1 ↔ ∀ {a b}, a ∈ s → b ∈ s → a = b := by
690   grind [card_le_one]

692 theorem card_le_one_iff_subsingleton_coe : #s ≤ 1 ↔ Subsingleton (s : Type _) :=
693   card_le_one.trans (s : Set α).subsingleton_coe.symm

695 /-- A finset has cardinality at most 1 iff its underlying set is subsingleton. -/
696 theorem card_le_one_iff_subsingleton : #s ≤ 1 ↔ (s : Set α).Subsingleton := by
697   rw [card_le_one_iff_subsingleton_coe, ← Set.subsingleton_coe, SetLike.coe_sort_coe]
698 
699 theorem card_le_one_iff_subset_singleton [Nonempty α] : #s ≤ 1 ↔ ∃ x : α, s ⊆ {x} := by
700   refine ⟨fun H => ?_, ?_⟩
701   · obtain rfl | ⟨x, hx⟩ := s.eq_empty_or_nonempty
702     · exact ⟨Classical.arbitrary α, empty_subset _⟩
703     · exact ⟨x, fun y hy => by rw [card_le_one.1 H y hy x hx, mem_singleton]⟩
704   · rintro ⟨x, hx⟩
705     rw [← card_singleton x]
706     exact card_le_card hx

708 lemma exists_mem_ne (hs : 1 < #s) (a : α) : ∃ b ∈ s, b ≠ a := by
709   have : Nonempty α := ⟨a⟩
710   by_contra!
711   exact hs.not_ge (card_le_one_iff_subset_singleton.2 ⟨a, subset_singleton_iff'.2 this⟩)
712 
713 /-- A `Finset` of a subsingleton type has cardinality at most one. -/
714 theorem card_le_one_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton α] (s : Finset α) : #s ≤ 1 :=
715   Finset.card_le_one_iff.2 fun {_ _ _ _} => Subsingleton.elim _ _

717 theorem one_lt_card : 1 < #s ↔ ∃ a ∈ s, ∃ b ∈ s, a ≠ b := by
718   contrapose!; exact card_le_one

720 theorem one_lt_card_iff : 1 < #s ↔ ∃ a b, a ∈ s ∧ b ∈ s ∧ a ≠ b := by
721   rw [one_lt_card]
722   simp only [exists_and_left]

724 theorem one_lt_card_iff_nontrivial : 1 < #s ↔ s.Nontrivial := by

726     not_nontrivial_iff_subsingleton, card_le_one_iff_subsingleton_coe, coe_sort_coe]

728 /-- If a Finset in a Pi type is nontrivial (has at least two elements), then
729   its projection to some factor is nontrivial, and the fibers of the projection
730   are proper subsets. -/
731 lemma exists_of_one_lt_card_pi {ι : Type*} {α : ι → Type*} [∀ i, DecidableEq (α i)]
732     {s : Finset (∀ i, α i)} (h : 1 < #s) :
733     ∃ i, 1 < #(s.image (· i)) ∧ ∀ ai, s.filter (· i = ai) ⊂ s := by
734   simp_rw [one_lt_card_iff, Function.ne_iff] at h ⊢
735   obtain ⟨a1, a2, h1, h2, i, hne⟩ := h
736   refine ⟨i, ⟨_, _, mem_image_of_mem _ h1, mem_image_of_mem _ h2, hne⟩, fun ai => ?_⟩
737   rw [filter_ssubset]
738   obtain rfl | hne := eq_or_ne (a2 i) ai
739   exacts [⟨a1, h1, hne⟩, ⟨a2, h2, hne⟩]

742     #s = n + 1 ↔ ∃ a t, ∃ (h : a ∉ t), cons a t h = s ∧ #t = n :=

777 theorem two_lt_card_iff : 2 < #s ↔ ∃ a b c, a ∈ s ∧ b ∈ s ∧ c ∈ s ∧ a ≠ b ∧ a ≠ c ∧ b ≠ c := by
778   classical
779     simp_rw [lt_iff_add_one_le, le_card_iff_exists_subset_card, reduceAdd, card_eq_three,
780       ← exists_and_left, exists_comm (α := Finset α)]

782     · rintro ⟨a, b, c, t, hsub, hab, hac, hbc, rfl⟩
783       exact ⟨a, b, c, by simp_all [insert_subset_iff]⟩
784     · rintro ⟨a, b, c, ha, hb, hc, hab, hac, hbc⟩
785       exact ⟨a, b, c, {a, b, c}, by simp_all [insert_subset_iff]⟩

791     ∃ a b c d, a ∈ s ∧ b ∈ s ∧ c ∈ s ∧ d ∈ s ∧
792     a ≠ b ∧ a ≠ c ∧ a ≠ d ∧ b ≠ c ∧ b ≠ d ∧ c ≠ d := by

806 /-! ### Inductions -/
807 
808 
809 /-- Suppose that, given objects defined on all strict subsets of any finset `s`, one knows how to
810 define an object on `s`. Then one can inductively define an object on all finsets, starting from
811 the empty set and iterating. This can be used either to define data, or to prove properties. -/
812 def strongInduction {p : Finset α → Sort*} (H : ∀ s, (∀ t ⊂ s, p t) → p s) :
813     ∀ s : Finset α, p s
814   | s =>
815     H s fun t h =>
816       have : #t < #s := card_lt_card h
817       strongInduction H t
818   termination_by s => #s
819 
820 theorem strongInduction_eq {p : Finset α → Sort*} (H : ∀ s, (∀ t ⊂ s, p t) → p s)
821     (s : Finset α) : strongInduction H s = H s fun t _ => strongInduction H t := by
822   rw [strongInduction]
823 
824 /-- Analogue of `strongInduction` with order of arguments swapped. -/
825 @[elab_as_elim]
826 def strongInductionOn {p : Finset α → Sort*} (s : Finset α) :
827     (∀ s, (∀ t ⊂ s, p t) → p s) → p s := fun H => strongInduction H s
828 
829 theorem strongInductionOn_eq {p : Finset α → Sort*} (s : Finset α)
830     (H : ∀ s, (∀ t ⊂ s, p t) → p s) :
831     s.strongInductionOn H = H s fun t _ => t.strongInductionOn H := by
832   dsimp only [strongInductionOn]
833   rw [strongInduction]
834 
835 @[elab_as_elim]
836 theorem case_strong_induction_on [DecidableEq α] {p : Finset α → Prop} (s : Finset α) (h₀ : p ∅)
837     (h₁ : ∀ a s, a ∉ s → (∀ t ⊆ s, p t) → p (insert a s)) : p s :=
838   Finset.strongInductionOn s fun s =>
839     Finset.induction_on s (fun _ => h₀) fun a s n _ ih =>
840       (h₁ a s n) fun t ss => ih _ (lt_of_le_of_lt ss (ssubset_insert n) : t < _)
841 
842 /-- Suppose that, given objects defined on all nonempty strict subsets of any nontrivial finset `s`,
843 one knows how to define an object on `s`. Then one can inductively define an object on all finsets,
844 starting from singletons and iterating.
845 
846 TODO: Currently this can only be used to prove properties.
847 Replace `Finset.Nonempty.exists_eq_singleton_or_nontrivial` with computational content
848 in order to let `p` be `Sort`-valued. -/
849 @[elab_as_elim]
850 protected lemma Nonempty.strong_induction {p : ∀ s, s.Nonempty → Prop}
851     (h₀ : ∀ a, p {a} (singleton_nonempty _))
852     (h₁ : ∀ ⦃s⦄ (hs : s.Nontrivial), (∀ t ht, t ⊂ s → p t ht) → p s hs.nonempty) :
853     ∀ ⦃s : Finset α⦄ (hs), p s hs
854   | s, hs => by
855     obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ | hs := hs.exists_eq_singleton_or_nontrivial
856     · exact h₀ _
857     · refine h₁ hs fun t ht hts ↦ ?_
858       have := card_lt_card hts
859       exact ht.strong_induction h₀ h₁
860 termination_by s => #s

862 /-- Suppose that, given that `p t` can be defined on all supersets of `s` of cardinality less than
863 `n`, one knows how to define `p s`. Then one can inductively define `p s` for all finsets `s` of
864 cardinality less than `n`, starting from finsets of card `n` and iterating. This
865 can be used either to define data, or to prove properties. -/
866 def strongDownwardInduction {p : Finset α → Sort*} {n : ℕ}
867     (H : ∀ t₁, (∀ {t₂ : Finset α}, #t₂ ≤ n → t₁ ⊂ t₂ → p t₂) → #t₁ ≤ n → p t₁) :
868     ∀ s : Finset α, #s ≤ n → p s
869   | s =>
870     H s fun {t} ht h =>
871       have := Finset.card_lt_card h
872       have : n - #t < n - #s := by lia
873       strongDownwardInduction H t ht
874   termination_by s => n - #s
875 
876 theorem strongDownwardInduction_eq {p : Finset α → Sort*}
877     (H : ∀ t₁, (∀ {t₂ : Finset α}, #t₂ ≤ n → t₁ ⊂ t₂ → p t₂) → #t₁ ≤ n → p t₁)
878     (s : Finset α) :
879     strongDownwardInduction H s = H s fun {t} ht _ => strongDownwardInduction H t ht := by
880   rw [strongDownwardInduction]
881 
882 /-- Analogue of `strongDownwardInduction` with order of arguments swapped. -/
883 @[elab_as_elim]
884 def strongDownwardInductionOn {p : Finset α → Sort*} (s : Finset α)
885     (H : ∀ t₁, (∀ {t₂ : Finset α}, #t₂ ≤ n → t₁ ⊂ t₂ → p t₂) → #t₁ ≤ n → p t₁) :
886     #s ≤ n → p s :=
887   strongDownwardInduction H s
888 
889 theorem strongDownwardInductionOn_eq {p : Finset α → Sort*} (s : Finset α)
890     (H : ∀ t₁, (∀ {t₂ : Finset α}, #t₂ ≤ n → t₁ ⊂ t₂ → p t₂) → #t₁ ≤ n → p t₁) :
891     s.strongDownwardInductionOn H = H s fun {t} ht _ => t.strongDownwardInductionOn H ht := by
892   dsimp only [strongDownwardInductionOn]
893   rw [strongDownwardInduction]
894 
895 theorem lt_wf {α} : WellFounded (@LT.lt (Finset α) _) :=
896   have H : Subrelation (@LT.lt (Finset α) _) (InvImage (· < ·) card) := fun {_ _} hxy =>
897     card_lt_card hxy
898   Subrelation.wf H <| InvImage.wf _ <| (Nat.lt_wfRel).2

900 /--
901 To prove a proposition for an arbitrary `Finset α`,
902 it suffices to prove that for any `S : Finset α`, the following is true:
903 the property is true for S with any element `s` removed, then the property holds for `S`.
904 
905 This is a weaker version of `Finset.strongInduction`.
906 But it can be more precise when the induction argument
907 only requires removing single elements at a time.
908 -/
909 theorem eraseInduction [DecidableEq α] {p : Finset α → Prop}
910     (H : (S : Finset α) → (∀ s ∈ S, p (S.erase s)) → p S) (S : Finset α) : p S :=
911   S.strongInduction fun S ih => H S fun _ hs => ih _ (erase_ssubset hs)

913 end Finset
